prompt: A flagpole is $30$ ft tall and casts a shadow $40$ ft long on level ground. What is the angle of elevation of the sun, in degrees, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: The pole and its shadow are the two legs of a right triangle. Which trig ratio uses the opposite and adjacent sides only?

hints.text: The pole and its shadow are the two legs of a right triangle. Which trig ratio uses the opposite and adjacent sides only?
Tangent is opposite over adjacent, so $\tan \theta = \frac{30}{40} = 0.75$. Use the inverse tangent key to turn the ratio back into an angle.
$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.75) \approx 36.9^\circ$, so the sun's angle of elevation is about $36.9^\circ$.

explanation: The angle of elevation is at the tip of the shadow, between the ground and the line of sight to the top of the pole.
From that angle the pole is the opposite side and the shadow is the adjacent side, so $\tan \theta = \frac{30}{40} = 0.75$.
The inverse tangent undoes the ratio: $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.75) \approx 36.9^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate before you press buttons
steps: The shadow is longer than the pole, so the angle must be less than $45^\circ$ (at exactly $45^\circ$ they would be equal).
$36.9^\circ$ passes that check; anything above $45^\circ$ would mean you flipped the fraction.
